svg.title: What each algorithm returns on the same graph
svg.desc: The UHG to Merlin Park graph drawn four times, once per algorithm. Breadth-first search returns O F G L N S D at cost 32, the route with the fewest roads rather than the cheapest. Hill climbing preferring the cheapest road walks O C A B and stops in the cul-de-sac at cost 5, never reaching the goal. Hill climbing preferring the most expensive road reaches the goal along O F G I J N S D at cost 39, the worst of the four routes. Uniform-cost search returns O F G L N Q R S D at cost 28, the cheapest route, having expanded twenty junctions against breadth-first search fifteen. Only uniform-cost search uses the accumulated cost of the whole path.
svg.text: ONE GRAPH, FOUR ALGORITHMS · THE ROUTE EACH ONE RETURNS
Same junctions, same roads, same costs. Only the rule for choosing changes.
uses: counts roads, ignores their cost
O → F → G → L → N → S → D
the fewest roads, and not the cheapest route
uses: one road ahead, nothing further
cheap roads led into the cul-de-sac
uses: one road ahead, nothing further
O → F → G → I → J → N → S → D
reached the goal along the worst of the four routes
uses: the cost of the whole path so far
O → F → G → L → N → Q → R → S → D
the cheapest route, and the most work done
Only the last rule weighs the cost of the whole path so far. It is also the one that expands the most junctions.
